text:
Talia Benson: Kicking off status page transparency upgrades. Goal for this thread: (1) confirm owners, (2) link the Linear epic, (3) align on what “component granularity” means for oncall (so we don’t end up with 1 giant “API” component again).

Talia Benson: Linear epic is here: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/status-page-transparency-upgrades (please subscribe). Product PRD: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-913/status-page-transparency-upgrades

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Thanks Talia. This one’s been coming up in every enterprise call. Let’s keep it customer-readable, not “internal services bingo”.

Rafael Mendes: I can be DRI from SRE side (delivery). Need a couple owners for taxonomy + mapping guidelines + runbook update.

Christine Wong: I can own implementation for status component changes (actual status page config + migration plan). Happy to co-own taxonomy draft w/ someone from oncall/runbooks.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll take runbook + oncall readiness (procedure, examples). Can also co-own taxonomy definitions as long as we agree what “granularity” means.

Miles Thornton: I’ll own incident-bot changes (guided prompts + status sync). Will need final list of components + required fields per update.

Marissa Cole: Product can help w/ naming + hierarchy (esp Console + rollouts side). But would like a clear principle: what does an oncall pick at 3am without overthinking.

Paula Mendes: +1. Also need consistency w/ Support macros (so they don’t say “API is down” when it’s just streaming disconnects).

Dev Patel: From Support: biggest pain is when status says “API degraded” and customers reply “which endpoint / which region / is it embeddings?” We need components that answer those questions directly.

Talia Benson: Great. Tentative ownership:
- Taxonomy + mapping guidelines: Christine + Tomáš (review: Rafael/Sean, plus Marissa/Paula for naming)
- Incident-bot automation: Miles (w/ Devon Price once we get to implementation)
- Update cadence/SLA + approvals: Rafael (consult Sean + Security later)
- Support alignment/macros: Paula + Dev

Rafael Mendes: Works for me.

Christine Wong: Works. Can we define “granularity” right now so I draft the taxonomy in the right shape?

Tomáš Novák: Yes pls. Otherwise we’ll boil the ocean.

Talia Benson: Cool, let’s pin a definition. What I’ve heard from previous incidents: “granularity” should map to *customer-observable surfaces* and *common partial failures*.

Sean Gallagher: Exactly. Not “scheduler-service” or “kv-cache-daemon”. Components should answer: “what’s impacted?” + “what can I do?”

Marissa Cole: Can we explicitly say: components = things customers recognize from docs/console? e.g. Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank, Console, Control Plane, etc.

Rafael Mendes: Yup. And we should support regional scoping where it matters (us-east vs eu-west) so customers can reroute.

Miles Thornton: Also need to decide when we allow multiple components per incident. Bot can nudge people but we need rules.

Tomáš Novák: Proposal (for oncall):
1) Default to the narrowest customer-facing component that matches the symptom.
2) Add region component only when impact is region-bound (metrics/alerts confirm) OR mitigation is “use another region”.
3) Avoid selecting every component “just in case”. If uncertain, pick the most likely + say what we’re checking.

Christine Wong: +1. Concrete example: “streaming keepalive timeouts” should be Streaming (and maybe Hosted API - us-east) but not Embeddings.

Dev Patel: For customers, if chat works but streaming breaks, they want to know “non-streaming requests OK”. So Streaming needs to be separate.

Paula Mendes: Also separate Console. We’ve had incidents where inference was fine but Console graphs were broken and customers thought the platform was down.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s anchor on this: if the workaround is “disable streaming” or “switch to non-streaming”, that’s *Streaming component*, not “API is down”.

Rafael Mendes: For “component granularity” I’d write it like:
- Minimum: separate by major product surface (Hosted API, Console, Dedicated control plane, Private control plane)
- Within Hosted API: separate by capability where partial degradation is common (Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank, maybe “Text generation (non-streaming)”)
- Add region breakdown for Hosted API serving where we can confidently detect (us-east/us-west/eu-west)

Christine Wong: Question: do we need “API Gateway” vs “Serving” split? Customers might not care, but it changes mitigation (retry/backoff vs switch model/region).

Sean Gallagher: I’m wary of “API Gateway” as a public component name. But a “Request Routing & Rate Limits” / “Capacity & Routing” type component might be more customer-friendly.

Marissa Cole: Agree. “Gateway” makes people think networking/VPN. “Capacity & Routing” matches what customers feel (429s, queueing, regional saturation).

Miles Thornton: For bot prompts, I can implement a question like: “Is impact limited to streaming? embeddings? rerank? console?” and “Is impact regional?” and then it suggests components.

Tomáš Novák: For oncall: we should keep the pick-list short enough. If we have 40 components no one will select correctly.

Christine Wong: Maybe we do hierarchy:
- Hosted API (global)
  - Streaming
  - Embeddings
  - Rerank
  - Capacity & Routing
  - Regions (us-east/us-west/eu-west) under Hosted API Serving
- Console
- Dedicated (Control Plane)
- Private (Control Plane)

Rafael Mendes: + add “Model Catalog / Model availability” as a component? Model-family-specific issues come up.

Sean Gallagher: That’s valid but keep it customer-safe. “Model availability” is fine; don’t expose internal model routing names.

Dev Patel: Also please: component names should match what Support can copy/paste without translating.

Talia Benson: Summarizing decisions for kickoff (tell me if wrong):
- “Component granularity” = customer-facing surfaces that can degrade independently + align with customer mitigations (retry/backoff, disable streaming, switch region/model).
- We will not expose internal service names.
- We will support region-scoped status for Hosted API serving when impact is region-bound.
- We’ll allow multiple components but with guidance to avoid “select all”; prefer narrow + explicit uncertainty language.

Paula Mendes: Looks right.

Marissa Cole: Yep. I’ll ask Design to sanity check naming once we have draft list.

Christine Wong: Next step: Tomáš + I will draft taxonomy list + definitions and share in Confluence for comments. Aim EOW.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll also start a runbook section “Choosing components: examples” (streaming-only failures, 429s/capacity, embeddings latency spikes, console outage).

Miles Thornton: Once taxonomy is stable-ish, I’ll start the incident-bot guided prompt flow behind a feature flag.

Incident Bot: Reminder set by Miles Thornton: “Follow up on status component taxonomy draft” at 2024-06-21 10:00 AM.

Rafael Mendes: One more: can we add a note on approvals? Like: oncall can publish initial updates without waiting, but post-incident summaries need review.

Sean Gallagher: Agree, but let’s keep that in a separate policy doc. For now: speed > perfection for initial update, as long as it’s accurate about what we know/don’t know.

Talia Benson: Great. I’ll capture this in the project plan + link this thread there. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
